title: The question of the sons. With the two mothers dead and Prince Yūsuf away at the court of Aragon, the old quarrel between Ismāʿīl's party and Yūsuf's has cooled. The next generation is harder. The crown prince's eldest, Muḥammad, is stubborn and unfit to rule; his second, Saʿd, is intelligent and studious. But Yūsuf's son, another Saʿd, four years old and raised at Benabarre, outshines them both, and the Emperor has grown set on raising this grandson at his own court

yusufsSon.Saʿd (b. 1394, by Caterina de Borja): child_gifted, 11/14/18, expensive in-depth education, at the Aragonese court

data.aragon: King Rodrigo (b. 1381); heir his sister Caterina, Yūsuf's wife, who is with child; the boy's own place in the Aragonese succession is not shown in the save
data.yusuf: living at the Aragonese court since his marriage (by January 1394); Trent counts the move a quirk of the game's marriages and is looking at moving him back

succession.note: the line as primogeniture orders it, sons before daughters and the elder line first; the game's other heir selections include Favored Son Succession, in which the ruler names any of his sons regardless of age
succession.favoredSonOption: open to al-Andalus, at a cost of 50 stability and 50 legitimacy (Trent); in September 1398 stability stood at 13.3 and legitimacy at 100

title: The Emperor calls his son Yūsuf and his grandson Saʿd home from Benabarre to the court at Ishbīliya, where the boy will be raised under his grandfather's eye. Caterina, heir of Aragon, stays at her brother's court

data.how: moved back with the Script Runner (move_country), undoing the game's move of a husband to his wife's court (Trent)
data.staysInAragon: Caterina de Borja, heir to King Rodrigo, with child by Yūsuf
